candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis is osteosarcoma, a primary malignant neoplasm. ALTR (pseudotumor) is a non-neoplastic inflammatory/reactive process associated with metal-on-metal bearings and elevated cobalt/chromium levels. The clinical record notes a ceramic-on-ceramic articulation (not metal-on-metal) and normal serum cobalt/chromium levels, making ALTR less supported, but regardless, ALTR and osteosarcoma are fundamentally different diagnostic entities with incompatible pathophysiology, treatment, and prognosis. C001 cannot be considered equivalent, a parent, or a component of osteosarcoma.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: ALTR/pseudotumor is a metal-ion hypersensitivity/wear-debris reaction; osteosarcoma is a primary malignant bone-forming tumor — these are distinct diagnostic entities

case_quality_flags: Reference diagnosis of osteosarcoma in a periprosthetic soft-tissue mass without bony involvement or bone-marrow edema on MRI is atypical; conventional osteosarcoma typically arises from bone. A periprosthetic extraskeletal osteosarcoma or soft-tissue osteosarcoma would be an unusual but recognized entity in this context.

Elevated alkaline phosphatase (318 IU/L) and large soft-tissue mass with negative cultures support a neoplastic process, but the absence of bony involvement makes classic osteosarcoma an uncommon reference choice; extraskeletal osteosarcoma or another sarcoma (e.g., undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma) might be considered.
Ceramic-on-ceramic bearing makes ALTR/pseudotumor less likely, consistent with normal cobalt/chromium levels.
